title: Zasocitinib, computationally designed by Nimbus with Schrodinger's platform, beats deucravacitinib in phase 3; FDA priority review
summary: TYK2 inhibitor designed on Schrodinger's computational platform: PASI 100 36.5% vs 13.9% for deucravacitinib at week 16 (LATITUDE Atlas, n=606); FDA accepted the NDA under priority review, Sep 2026.
account: HCPLive (30 September 2026, EADV) reported LATITUDE Atlas (NCT06973291), in which 606 adults were randomized 301/303. At week 16, zasocitinib versus deucravacitinib gave PASI 100 36.5% vs 13.9%, PASI 90 62.5% vs 34.0% and sPGA 0 43.2% vs 18.5% (p<.001). Linda Stein Gold presented the results. pharmaphorum (15 September 2026) reported Food and Drug Administration (FDA) acceptance of the marketing application under priority review, with a decision expected mid-March 2027. The phase 2b trial (Armstrong et al., JAMA Dermatology 2024; 259 treated patients) reached PASI 75 in 67–68% at 15–30 mg versus 6% on placebo. It was funded by Nimbus Discovery, with Nimbus and Takeda affiliations among the authors. The discovery claim comes from the developers' side. Takeda's dermatology medical head told Drug Target Review (26 September 2025) that Nimbus chemists “used an AI-assisted approach of computationally guided structure-based drug design”. GEN (18 August 2023) reported a Nimbus-Schrodinger paper on “computational physics-based predictions” in identifying NDI-034858. BioPharma Dive (13 December 2022) reported Takeda's $4 billion upfront purchase. No regulatory approval had been granted as of 20 October 2026.
purpose: Design a selective oral allosteric TYK2 inhibitor for plaque psoriasis and other immune-mediated diseases
system: Schrodinger physics-based computational drug-design platform with machine learning, used by Nimbus Therapeutics to discover NDI-034858 (TAK-279, zasocitinib)
location: United States (Nimbus, Boston; Takeda Development Center Americas, Cambridge, MA); phase 2b at 55 sites in the US and Canada; phase 3 sites unverified

ratings.reason: Trial participants achieved complete skin clearance at higher rates. PASI 100 was 36.5% vs 13.9% at week 16 in LATITUDE Atlas, and 33% at 30 mg in phase 2b.
Takeda's new drug application was accepted under FDA priority review in September 2026, after a $4 billion upfront acquisition of the program.
No approval or population-level outcome as of 20 October 2026.

ai_role.statement: The sources include only developer-side accounts of the discovery method: Takeda's medical head in Drug Target Review, and GEN citing a Nimbus-Schrodinger paper. They describe AI-assisted, physics-based structure-based design, not a pure machine-learning discovery. The clinical results come from a Nimbus-funded randomized trial and from Takeda-presented phase 3 data reported by HCPLive and pharmaphorum. No independent account of the computational platform's contribution was found.
